subject.title: [Feature]: Add one-way dispatch mode for A2A handoffs without reply-back ping-pong

question: Should OpenClaw add a first-party one-way A2A dispatch contract now, and should it be a `sessions_send` mode/flag or a separate `sessions_deliver`-style primitive?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix changes model-facing tool API and session delivery semantics across A2A workflows, so automation should not choose the public contract shape or default behavior.

options.title: Add an explicit dispatch mode
options.body: Keep current `sessions_send` behavior as default and add an additive dispatch-only mode or flag with tests proving no requester reinjection or announce occurs.

options.title: Create a separate primitive
options.body: Introduce a new one-way delivery tool so conversation and dispatch semantics cannot be confused, at the cost of another model-visible tool surface.

options.title: Defer to broader handoff work
options.body: Keep this open as acceptance criteria for a broader A2A handoff contract that also covers structured skip, routing, and thread inheritance.

recommendation.title: Add an explicit dispatch mode
recommendation.body: Keep current `sessions_send` behavior as default and add an additive dispatch-only mode or flag with tests proving no requester reinjection or announce occurs.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history and maintainer-scoping signal for session tool and handoff API direction.
